archetype.name: Game Manager (veteran QB3)
archetype.definition: A 14-year undrafted journeyman who wins on timing, footwork and quick, short-to-intermediate reads inside a structured scheme. He can run a good offense for a week or two, but he can't carry a bad situation.

report.headline: A good spot start and a bad relief cameo, now parked at QB3
report.take:
Case Keenum is what he has been for most of a long career: a quick-processing, low-aggression distributor who lives on schedule. His time to throw (2.65), aggressiveness (13.21%) and intended air yards (7.44) all sit in the same band as his 2017-2019 seasons. The one year he rose above that, 2017 in Minnesota, came with a strong supporting cast, a +3.584 CPOE and a 0.174 EPA per play. Nearly every other season his accuracy over expected was negative. In 2026 he is insurance. Caleb Williams has started every game since Week 6, and as of November 3 Keenum is the Bears' QB3, inactive as the emergency third quarterback.

His two games tell the story of his ceiling and his floor. In the Week 3 start against Philadelphia, a defense now ranked 29th, he was pressured on only 8.6% of dropbacks and had a bad-throw rate of 8.8%. He posted 7.3 passing EPA, 0.213 EPA per dropback and a 2.8 CPOE in a 27-7 win. Ben Johnson's offense carried him there. Under center he was 92.9% with 0.818 EPA a play and an 85.7% success rate. From shotgun he sat at -0.394 EPA a play. Play-action and the timing game from under center did the heavy lifting.

In Green Bay he came in for a third of the snaps of a 7-31 loss, against a defense now ranked 7th. He threw from behind in obvious passing downs, and it fell apart: -6.4 EPA, a 31.6% bad-throw rate, a pick, a lost fumble and two sacks. His trailing-by-9-plus split (-11.9 EPA total) holds most of the damage. That fits who he is: when the script forces him to drive the ball rather than distribute it, he has nothing extra to reach for.

The season line is the two games blended: 0.015 EPA per dropback (27th of 47), slightly below league average almost across the board. Only a 3.6% sack rate (4th) is a real plus. The honest read is that he's a competent short-term fill-in in a good scheme against a soft defense, and a liability against a good one. Right now he's not expected to play at all.

strengths.title: Operates Johnson's under-center play-action game
strengths.body: On 14 under-center plays he was nearly flawless, against a badly negative shotgun split. That is the scheme's play-action and boot game giving a veteran with good timing defined reads and open windows. The sample is small, but it matches what Keenum has always needed: structure, not improvisation.

strengths.title: Intermediate middle-of-field timing throws
strengths.body: His best work came 10-19 yards down the field and between the numbers. Those are the in-breakers and digs where anticipation matters more than arm. Eleven intermediate attempts produced 8.1 EPA, and the middle of the field holds both his touchdowns. It is a small sample, but it's consistent with his 2017 profile as a rhythm thrower over the middle.

strengths.title: Gets the ball out, avoids sacks
strengths.body: His 3.6% sack rate ranks 4th and sits 3.3 points under league average. Ranking 2nd in pressured percentage shows the quick release keeps the rush off him. That is a stable trait: his pressure-to-sack rates in 2018 and 2019 were also among the better marks of those seasons.

concerns.title: Collapses when forced to chase games
concerns.body: Trailing by nine or more, his dropbacks cost 11.9 EPA. Within one score, he added 10.2. That split is mostly the Green Bay relief stint, but it reflects a real limitation. Without a vertical arm or creation off script, obvious passing downs expose the inaccuracy behind his 31.6% bad-throw rate that day. Over his career he has rarely produced positive accuracy over expected, so this is closer to who he is than a blip.

concerns.title: Short game and deep ball both leak value
concerns.body: Thirty-two short throws averaged -0.117 EPA despite a 68.8% completion rate, which means checkdowns and failed underneath completions. Four deep shots returned -0.816 a play. The deep number is too few attempts to judge on its own, but a 38-year-old with a career aDOT in the 7s isn't going to become a downfield passer. The short-area inefficiency is the bigger issue for a quarterback whose game is built there.

concerns.title: No path to snaps behind Williams
concerns.body: He is listed as QB3 and was inactive as the emergency third quarterback. Williams has started three straight, and Bagent drew the Week 5 start ahead of him. Any meaningful 2026 production now requires two injuries in front of him.

trend.note: He went from a 7.3-EPA spot start against a soft Eagles defense to a -6.4-EPA relief stint in a blowout at Green Bay. He hasn't taken a meaningful snap since, as Williams reclaimed the job in Week 6.

nextGame.headline: Inactive as QB3; Tampa's defense would be a bad draw anyway
nextGame.body:
If he somehow played, Tampa Bay is close to his worst matchup. The Bucs rank 2nd in defensive EPA and 2nd against the pass, and they are 2nd at stopping short throws (-0.2 EPA), the exact zone Keenum lives in. They allow only 11.6 PPR points a game to quarterbacks (3rd). The one opening is a light pass rush: 28th in hit rate and 24th in sack rate. That would give him the clean pockets he had against Philadelphia, but clean pockets don't help much if the underneath windows are closed. Their soft spot, deep passing (19th), is the part of the field he doesn't attack.

Availability is the real story. Keenum is QB3 and was inactive as the emergency third quarterback. He only sees the field if Williams goes down and Bagent is unavailable, or in a late blowout. Chicago is a 6-point favorite, and Tampa is without WR Emeka Egbuka (86% of snaps) and LB Yaya Diaby. That makes a comfortable Bears lead more plausible than a scramble drill, but even mop-up duty would go to the QB2 first.

keyMatchups.title: Underneath passer vs. top short defense
keyMatchups.body: Keenum's game is short and intermediate timing. Tampa allows almost nothing on short throws and ranks 2nd against the pass overall. His short-throw EPA was already negative against easier opponents.

keyMatchups.title: Weak Bucs rush, clean pockets
keyMatchups.body: Tampa rarely hits the quarterback. His best game came when he was barely pressured, and his worst when the pocket got muddy and he was behind. This is the one way the matchup bends his way.

keyMatchups.title: Game script favors Chicago
keyMatchups.body: With Chicago a 6-point favorite and Tampa's offense 30th in passing EPA, Chicago is likely to play from ahead. That is the only scenario where a QB3 sees garbage snaps, and even then they'd likely go to the backup first.

nextGame.watch: Whether Keenum stays inactive as the emergency third QB. Any change to Caleb Williams' status is the only thing that makes this game relevant to him.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect little to nothing. Williams is the starter, and Keenum sits behind a QB2, so his realistic weekly projection is zero snaps. If injuries push him into a start, the Week 3 template is the best case: a clean pocket, under-center play-action and middle-of-the-field timing throws against a soft defense. That could produce something like 170-240 yards with one or two touchdowns. Against a good defense, or once the Bears fall behind, the Green Bay version is more likely.

Of his traits, the low sack rate and quick release are sustainable; they've been part of his game for years. The under-center efficiency and the hot intermediate numbers rest on a handful of plays and would cool over a longer run. His accuracy over expected should settle back near his slightly negative career norm. Treat him purely as an emergency handcuff with a modest floor in this scheme, not as someone who will produce on his own.
swingFactors: Whether Bagent stays ahead of him at QB2
Opponent strength if he does start

confidence.note: Two games and 57 dropbacks, split between a start and a blowout relief stint, and he's now inactive at QB3.
